title: Previews that resolve through the shell thumbnail cost 40-53 ms on every request when no thumbnail can be produced
body:
## What happens

File types the preview host draws through the shell thumbnail path — Office documents, PDF,
DWG/DXF, everything listed in `IsKnownShellPreview` — are cheap when a thumbnail exists and
expensive when one cannot be produced.

Pulse 1.0.33, Windows 11 x64. Timed around each preview-host request (`Pulse.Preview.exe` reused
across requests, `pixel_size` = 512):

| File | First request | Repeat requests | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PDF that has a thumbnail | 72.8 ms | **5.5 ms** | bitmap (system cache hit) |
| XLSX with no thumbnail | **231.6 ms** | **41.5 ms** | `provider-failed` |
| PDF with no thumbnail (CAD export) | **264.6 ms** | **53.1 ms** | `provider-failed` |

For scale, on the same machine and run: a WIC-decoded BMP costs ~12 ms, plain text ~0.25 ms.

The repeat numbers are the interesting part. Once a failure has been established, every later
request for the same file still pays 40-53 ms, because nothing durable remembers the failure.
Opening a folder holding thirty such files queues roughly 1.2 s of background work, which shows up
as thumbnails trickling in.

## Why: `MakeShellThumbnail` runs every fallback even when all of them fail

`MakeShellThumbnail` in `src/preview_host/main.cpp` tries four sources in order and returns at the
first hit:

1. `FromThumbnailCache(..., cache_only = true)` — the system thumbnail cache, the cheap path.
2. `FromThumbnailProvider(...)` — binds `IThumbnailProvider`, which loads the Office/PDF handler
   into the host process.
3. `FromThumbnailCache(..., cache_only = false)` — `WTS_EXTRACT`, which may launch an external
   producer.
4. `IShellItemImageFactory::GetImage(...)` with `SIIGBF_THUMBNAILONLY`.

A success usually ends at step 1, which is why it costs 5.5 ms. A failure means steps 1, 2, 3 and 4
all ran, each creating COM objects and, for step 2, loading a heavyweight handler — that is the
40-53 ms floor. The first request on top of that pays the one-time handler load.

## Possible impact beyond the raw numbers

The preview pipe allows one second per request (`ThumbnailCache::Worker`), and a timeout there makes
the UI stop and restart the host. A restart drops every handler the host had loaded, so one
pathological file can make the next preview of an unrelated type slow as well. I have not
reproduced that chain directly — it is inferred from the code paths — but it would explain reports
of previews feeling slower after opening an awkward file.

## Reproducer

Any type in `IsKnownShellPreview` whose thumbnail provider is missing or rejects the file. Timing
each step inside `MakeShellThumbnail`, or a timer around a `PreviewRequest` sent over the pipe,
shows the four attempts running in sequence.

## Possible directions, each with a trade-off

- **Drop step 4.** `IShellItemImageFactory` overlaps steps 2 and 3 — it resolves through the same
  handler chain — so removing it takes one full attempt out of the failure path. Risk: a few cases
  that only `SIIGBF_THUMBNAILONLY` handles today would start returning `provider-failed`.
- **Remember negative results across sessions.** The UI-side `ThumbnailCache` LRU already caches the
  failure, but only in memory, so every restart retries. A small on-disk note keyed by
  path + mtime + size would remove the repeat cost entirely.
- **Give the failure path a shorter deadline.** The 1 s budget exists for legitimately slow
  extractions; a failure is detectable much sooner.

Happy to prototype any of these — the first is the smallest change.

comments.body:
Closing. The user-facing half of this - a handler that never returns stalling
the pane and taking every later preview down with it - is addressed by the
second commit of #10: a handler apartment that neither finishes its open nor
applies a command inside a 3 s budget is retired, the extension cools down to
the thumbnail path, and the next selection starts a fresh apartment, so a cold
provider costs at most its own file.

What remains from the measurements above is the per-file probe cost of a shell
thumbnail miss (all four fallbacks run in the preview host). That is background
work on a worker thread, and failures are already cached for the session on the
UI side, so each file pays it once - not worth the added bookkeeping for now.
Reopen if it ever shows up as more than that.
